feedback.problem: Calculate the points where the hyperbola $\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}=1$ intersects the line $x=-1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the points where the hyperbola intersects the line $x=-1,$ we substitute $x=-1$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ \frac{(-1)^{2}}{4}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ \frac{1}{4}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ -\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =\frac{3}{4} \\ {y}^{2} & =-\frac{27}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

We cannot take the square root of a negative number. Therefore, the equation has no real solutions. 
So, the hyperbola does not intersect the vertical line $x=-1.$

submitted_fields.submitted_value: There are no points of intersection
